newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Brent may gain, but faces firm resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Brent may gain, but faces firm resistance.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures have room to move higher on Wednesday after a strong showing yesterday with a potential bullish double bottom, but heavy resistance is visible around $18.50 a barrel.
August Brent, which expires later today, closed 58 cents stronger on Tuesday at $18.39 a barrel, while August gas oil was $2.75 a tonne firmer, traders and technical analysts said.

"Brent can go either way, but if it can open higher it could test resistance around $18.48/$18.50," said Darren Gurner at Sucden in London citing the 40 day moving average as an obstacle to pushing higher.

Steve Kwan at MMS also saw heavy resistance at $18.50 with a downward trendline of May 16 at $20.50 and July 2 at $18.96 converging with recent congestion over the last couple of days around this level.
The potential formation of a double bottom also looked positive.
"If it can get through $18.50 then there is crucial resistance around $19.00," said Kwan.
Support was seen around $18.00 which the market sees as a break point after the bounce yesterday off $17.80
"There's a strong possibility people will step back in to buy around this level," said one analyst.
Gurner saw nearby support at $18.08, then $18.00 and $17.80 with a previous June 18 low of $17.68 as further out support.

August gas oil may want to test resistance after successfully testing support on Tuesday, but a recent gap between $165.25 and $165.75 and congestion on July 4, July 9 and July 14 around $165.25 will act as a strong barrier. If this point is broken the 40 day moving average of $167.65 will act as a subsequent breach marker.
The low yesterday of $160.00 is set to be initial support, analysts said.
